The man who edited Dragon Ball for decades says its last anime should never have been approved.
packages.hook_line: Akira Toriyama's own editor called his final anime garbage.
packages.opening_sentence: Akira Toriyama's own editor called his final anime garbage.
packages.vo: Akira Toriyama's own editor called his final anime garbage. Kazuhiko Torishima, who shaped Dragon Ball from the start, said in Naples that Daima betrays the franchise, calls episode one useless, and has no idea how it was approved. He said the same thing back in 2025. But Daima wasn't a safe cash-grab sequel. Toriyama shrunk his own cast back to basics on purpose, right before he passed, closing the story his way instead of chasing scale. Fans noticed the gap: Daima merch still sells out, and the show keeps gaining fans months later. Is the editor protecting the legacy, or just wrong about it? Leave your take.
packages.question_line: Is the editor protecting the legacy, or just wrong about it?

packages.hook_line: Tanya the Evil just got dethroned, then took its crown right back.
packages.opening_sentence: Tanya the Evil just got dethroned, then took its crown right back.
packages.vo: Tanya the Evil just got dethroned, then took its crown right back. Week one of Summer 2026, Saga of Tanya the Evil II topped the season rankings. Week two, an underdog, Jaadugar: A Witch in Mongolia, jumped from third to first and knocked Tanya to fourth. Week three, Tanya reclaimed the top spot. That's not a fluke vote swing, that's a season surviving getting beaten. Most sequels lose momentum the second something newer shows up. Tanya's audience came right back once the hype settled. A war-isekai premise nobody expected to hold up nine years later is still winning. Does Tanya deserve the crown back? Leave your take.
